text:
Alex DeBrincat came into the season off a year in which Evolving-Hockey ranked him sixth among 401 forwards in wins above replacement. Lately he has looked like a different player, and Detroit has gone with him. One widely shared post framed it plainly: he and Viktor Arvidsson have gone cold, the Red Wings have fallen on hard times, and Todd McLellan won't let them sulk.

The slump is real but not alarming. Two goals in his last ten games, where we'd expect about eight points at his ice time. Our verdict is some of each: he is getting slightly fewer chances, and the ones he gets aren't going in. He is shooting 9.4% against a career-shaped range of 11 to 15.

The process underneath still looks like DeBrincat. Detroit takes 56% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on the ice, about 11 points better than without him, and he has 9.3 expected goals on his own shots. His Nov. 21 goal against the Islanders ended a drought; the chances say the last month undersells him.
headline: Alex DeBrincat's cold spell, and Detroit's
